steps.description: Implement a controlled numerical experiment to test the geometric hypothesis on solution-space rigidity using small feedforward networks. The script will: (1) Define a constraint function f(x) with known analytic properties; (2) Generate w training samples; (3) Train networks with varying hidden widths N; (4) Measure max absolute error on a held-out validation set; (5) Determine N_c(w) as the minimal width achieving zero violation (error ≤ 1e-3). The experiment will sweep w from 5 to 50 and N from 2 to 100, logging training/validation errors and N_c values. Results will be analyzed for rigidity (finite N_c constant in w) vs. fatness (N_c diverges or is unattainable).

Design and execute a numerical experiment to test the "geometry" hypothesis regarding solution space rigidity in small feedforward networks. Specifically: (1) define a family of analytic constraints (e.g., polynomial or trigonometric functions with known smoothness); (2) sample w constraint points; (3) sweep hidden layer width N from 4 to 64; (4) train network to minimize loss on training set; (5) evaluate max absolute error on held-out validation set; (6) record N_c(w) as minimum width achieving zero violation (error ≤ 1e-3); (7) repeat for multiple w values to assess scaling. Use standard activation (ReLU/Tanh), Adam optimizer, and sufficient training iterations to convergence. Plot N_c(w) vs w and assess whether N_c remains bounded (rigid) or grows unbounded (fat). Validate against literature on neural network capacity and Kolmogorov width.

Design a bootstrap experiment to probe solution space rigidity of small feedforward networks. Generate an analytic constraint function (e.g., a polynomial or trigonometric function) with known properties. Sweep constraint sample size w and hidden layer width N. For each (w, N) pair, train a small feedforward network on w points, evaluate maximum absolute error on a held-out test set of constraints. Record N_c(w) = minimum N achieving max error ≤ 1e3. Plot N_c vs w to determine if rigidity (bounded N_c) holds. Use fixed random seeds for reproducibility.

plans.objective: [DIM: optimization] The minimal network capacity N_c(w) follows a phase-transition scaling: for w < w_c (critical constraint density), N_c(w) remains constant (rigid regime), while for w > w_c, N_c(w) diverges exponentially with w (fat regime), reflecting a sharp transition in solution space accessibility.

steps.description: Implement a numerical experiment to test the phase-transition scaling hypothesis for minimal network capacity N_c(w) as a function of constraint density w. The experiment will: (1) Define a bootstrap constraint problem using a target function with known analytical constraints; (2) Systematically vary w (constraint count) and N (hidden layer width); (3) Train small feedforward networks to satisfy constraints; (4) Measure N_c(w) as the minimum width achieving zero violation (max absolute error ≤ 1e-3) on held-out constraints; (5) Analyze scaling behavior to identify rigid vs. fat regimes and critical w_c. The code will generate the required scan data, training/validation metrics, and N_c(w) values for analysis.
